reconcile.note: Keil and Delitzsch read Isaiah 1:13 as rejecting corrupt, hypocritical worship rather than repealing the Sabbath law that Exodus makes an everlasting covenant sign.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Julius Wellhausen argued the prophets, including Isaiah, never regarded the priestly festal calendar as divinely commanded in the first place, undercutting any harmony with Exodus 31.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Julius Wellhausen (1885), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1885).

sides.snippet: Therefore the children of Israel shall keep the Sabbath, to observe the Sabbath throughout their generations, for a perpetual covenant.
sides.verseText: Therefore the children of Israel shall keep the Sabbath, to observe the Sabbath throughout their generations, for a perpetual covenant.

sides.snippet: Bring no more vain offerings. Incense is an abomination to me; New moons, Sabbaths, and convocations: I can't bear with evil assemblies.
sides.verseText: Bring no more vain offerings. Incense is an abomination to me; New moons, Sabbaths, and convocations: I can't bear with evil assemblies.
